notes: rl2:AssetCollection with rl2:member → odrl:AssetCollection with odrl:partOf edges from each member, which travel with the policy into the corpus closure; rl2:subject on the clause → odrl:assignee on the permission. The grant itself translates directly. What does not carry over is RL2's direct-only matching: due2 closes partOf transitively (README, standing divergences), and there is no way to declare a collection non-transitive. To exercise this, the policy adds a nested collection ex:Registries (an AssetCollection inside ex:ClinicalOutcomes) with member ex:CancerRegistry: RL2 states nested collections are not expanded, so scenario 3 is NotApplicable in RL2 and Permit in due2. Scenarios 3 and 4 are added.

expected.why: ex:Demographics partOf ex:ClinicalOutcomes, an AssetCollection, so the target part holds; action and assignee match; ex:collectionAccess applies with no duties.
ex:Outcomes partOf ex:ClinicalOutcomes; the permission applies with no duties.

ex:CancerRegistry partOf ex:Registries partOf ex:ClinicalOutcomes; the path passes only through AssetCollections, and the closure is transitive, so ex:CancerRegistry ⊑ ex:ClinicalOutcomes and the permission applies.
No partOf path leads from ex:Genomics to ex:ClinicalOutcomes, so the target part is F and the permission does not apply; no other rule exists.
